scope: Latest active learner-v2 Philosophy topics: Indian Philosophy 01-05 and Philosophy of Religion 01-10

source_session_heading_references: Historical Reconstruction and the Source Problem
lines: CĀRVĀKA / LOKĀYATA: RECONSTRUCTION BEFORE DOCTRINE
v                   v                   v
lost Bṛhaspati-sūtra  opponent reports   quoted fragments
(Mādhava, Jayanta,  (often polemical)
Śāntarakṣita)
v
RULE: distinguish attested thesis from hostile caricature
Lokāyata = this-worldly orientation; Cārvāka = materialist school label.
VALID KNOWLEDGE (PRAMĀ)                     REJECTED INDEPENDENT SOURCES
v                                             v
PRATYAKṢA / PERCEPTION              anumāna     śabda      upamāna
direct, sense-grounded              inference   testimony  comparison
v                              v
observed conjunction is finite; universal vyāpti outruns perception
smoke seen with fire in kitchens != smoke is invariably fire-linked.
CĀRVĀKA ATTACK: inference needs universal concomitance (vyāpti)
vyāpti known by inference -> circularity | by perception -> incomplete survey
hidden condition (upādhi) may defeat the rule: fire without smoke, wet fuel matters
NYĀYA REPLY: repeated agreement + absence of counter-instance + tarka
anvaya (presence) + vyatireka (absence) -> defeasible but rational vyāpti
CĀRVĀKA COUNTER-PRESSURE: practical expectation may work without certainty
SELF-REFUTATION CHARGE: arguing against inference already employs inference.
ONLY THIS-WORLDLY ELEMENTS ARE REQUIRED
earth + water + fire + air -> organised living body -> consciousness
consciousness is a body-property, not an immaterial substance
analogy: fermentation ingredients -> intoxicating power not present separately
SELF = living conscious body (dehātma-vāda)
death -> elemental dissolution -> no surviving ātman, rebirth or afterlife
QUALIFICATION: emergence is asserted; a full mechanism is not supplied.
NO PERCEPTUAL WARRANT
+-> no immortal soul -> no rebirth
+-> no karma as supersensible moral force
+-> no heaven/hell -> no post-mortem reward or punishment
+-> no creator God -> world needs no transcendent planner
+-> no Vedic infallibility -> priestly testimony lacks intrinsic authority
RESULT: metaphysics is cut back to perceptible nature and embodied life.
PURUṢĀRTHA FILTER
dharma: rejected when grounded in unseen reward or Vedic command
mokṣa: rejected as liberation of a separable soul
artha + kāma: intelligible goods within one embodied life
prudent enjoyment != reckless indulgence
pleasure sought -> weigh pain, social consequence and attainable means
EXAM CONTROL: call it naturalistic hedonism or this-worldliness;
do not reduce the school to the hostile slogan “eat, drink and borrow.”
ISSUE          CĀRVĀKA             NYĀYA              BUDDHISM
pramāṇa        perception only     four pramāṇas      perception + inference
self           conscious body      enduring ātman     anātman stream
causation      observed sequence   realist relation   dependent origination
transcendent   denied              God, soul, karma   karma without creator
liberation     death ends person    apavarga           nirvāṇa
STRENGTH: anti-dogmatic evidential discipline
LIMIT: perception-only rule struggles to justify science, memory and its own critique.
DEFINE source problem -> STATE perception thesis -> RECONSTRUCT inference attack
v                         v                         v
explain upādhi/circularity -> give Nyāya reply -> assess self-refutation
v
derive materialism -> embodied self -> transcendent denials -> ethical result
v
QUALIFIED VERDICT: Cārvāka is a rigorous empiricist challenge, but its exclusive
pratyakṣa criterion is narrower than the reasoning needed to defend that challenge.
JAIN REALITY (SAT) = permanence-through-change
v                       v
JĪVA                     AJĪVA
conscious substances       non-conscious substances
innumerable souls          pudgala | dharma | adharma | ākāśa | kāla
v
each dravya has enduring substance + changing guṇa/paryāya
UTPĀDA + VYAYA + DHRAUVYA = origination + cessation + persistence.
JĪVA: consciousness (upayoga) is essential; knowledge is naturally unbounded
embodied state -> soul expands/contracts to body -> agency + experience
AJĪVA FIVEFOLD
pudgala = matter, including karmic matter | ākāśa = accommodation
dharma = medium of motion              | adharma = medium of rest
kāla = condition of change
TRAP: dharma/adharma here are cosmic media, not moral merit/demerit.
PASSIONATE ACTIVITY (yoga + kaṣāya)
v
ĀSRAVA: influx of subtle karmic pudgala into jīva
v
BANDHA: karmic matter binds and obscures knowledge, faith, energy, bliss
saṃvara blocks new influx + nirjarā sheds old karma
v
MOKṢA: kevala-jñāna; liberated siddha rises beyond saṃsāra.
REALITY HAS INNUMERABLE ASPECTS
v                             v
ANEKĀNTAVĀDA                     NAYAVĀDA
metaphysical many-sidedness      partial standpoints of judgement
v
SYĀDVĀDA: conditional predication — “in a certain respect”
partial statement can be valid without being absolutely exhaustive
TRAP: not scepticism; omniscience knows fully, finite knowers know perspectivally.
ABOUT OBJECT X, UNDER SPECIFIED STANDPOINT / TIME / MODE:
1 syād-asti              -> in some respect, X is
2 syān-nāsti             -> in some respect, X is not
3 syād-asti-nāsti        -> successively, X is and is not
4 syād-avaktavyaḥ        -> X is inexpressible under simultaneous demand
5 syād-asti-avaktavyaḥ   -> X is and is inexpressible
6 syān-nāsti-avaktavyaḥ  -> X is not and is inexpressible
7 syād-asti-nāsti-avaktavyaḥ -> X is, is not, and is inexpressible
CONTRADICTION IS AVOIDED BY DIFFERENT RESPECTS, NOT BY ASSERTING P AND NOT-P SIMPLY.
SAMYAG-DARŚANA -> SAMYAG-JÑĀNA -> SAMYAK-CĀRITRA
right faith          right knowledge      right conduct
five vows: ahiṃsā, satya, asteya,
brahmacarya, aparigraha
householder aṇuvrata -> ascetic mahāvrata -> guṇasthāna purification
ahiṃsā disciplines body, speech and thought because every jīva can be harmed.
OBJECTION                         JAIN REPLY
syādvāda is self-refuting           it applies conditionally to itself, not absolutely
seven forms are repetitive          combinations track affirmation, denial, ineffability
anekānta destroys truth             it rejects one-sided absolutism, not determinate truth
karma-matter/soul contact obscure   bondage is beginningless via passions and subtle pudgala
BUDDHISM: change without substance | VEDĀNTA: unity beneath plurality
JAINISM: real substances persist through real modes; plurality is irreducible.
OPEN: Jainism joins realism, pluralism and perspectival discipline
ontology -> jīva/ajīva -> dravya-guṇa-paryāya -> permanence-through-change
epistemology -> anekānta -> naya -> syāt -> exact seven bhaṅgas
soteriology -> karma as matter -> āsrava/bandha -> saṃvara/nirjarā -> mokṣa
evaluate strongest contradiction objection and standpoint reply
CLOSE: qualified predication protects complexity without surrendering truth.
COMMON THERAPEUTIC CORE
duḥkha -> origin (tṛṣṇā/avidyā) -> cessation (nirvāṇa) -> eightfold path
three marks: anitya | duḥkha | anātman
dependent origination supplies the middle way:
neither eternal substance nor causeless annihilation
later schools disagree about what exists and how it is known,
not about the need to end ignorance and craving.
avidyā -> saṃskāra -> vijñāna -> nāma-rūpa -> ṣaḍāyatana -> sparśa
-> vedanā -> tṛṣṇā -> upādāna -> bhava -> jāti -> jarā-maraṇa
IGNORANCE conditions formations; craving and grasping renew becoming
“When this is, that comes to be; with cessation of this, that ceases”
reverse order: end avidyā/tṛṣṇā -> break appropriation -> end rebirth-duḥkha.
PRATĪTYASAMUTPĀDA -> conditioned things arise and perish -> KṢAṆIKAVĀDA
causal efficacy belongs to the moment; no unchanged bearer is required
PERSON ANALYSIS -> five skandhas
rūpa | vedanā | saṃjñā | saṃskāra | vijñāna
none is permanent, independent or “mine” -> NAIRĀTMYAVĀDA
continuity = causal series, like flame-to-flame; identity is neither strict sameness
nor total unrelatedness.
NO ĀTMAN, YET CAUSAL RESPONSIBILITY
intention at t1 -> conditions stream -> fruit at t2
memory = later cognition causally conditioned by earlier experience
rebirth = one psycho-physical series conditions another, without soul-transmigration
objection: if agent perishes, another receives result
reply: successor is neither identical nor wholly different; causal appropriation connects
nirvāṇa = cessation of greed, hatred and delusion, not destruction of a substance-self.
BUDDHIST REALITY / KNOWLEDGE DEBATE
v                                             v
HĪNAYĀNA REALISTS                               MAHĀYĀNA
Vaibhāṣika     Sautrāntika                    Yogācāra    Mādhyamika
external       external objects               cognition   emptiness of
dharmas        inferred from ideas             only        all svabhāva
directly       and causal effects
perceived
SCHOOL LABELS MARK EPISTEMIC/ONTOLOGICAL POSITIONS, NOT FOUR PATHS TO MIX.
ISSUE              VAIBHĀṢIKA                  SAUTRĀNTIKA
external object    real dharmas                 real momentary causes
access             direct perception            inferred from mental image
past/future        sarvāstivāda: dharmas exist  only present causal moment stressed
cognition          grasps object                represents object
SAUTRĀNTIKA ARGUMENT: object-moment is gone when awareness occurs;
therefore cognition presents an image, from which external cause is inferred.
PRESSURE: representative realism must explain correspondence.
YOGĀCĀRA / VIJÑĀNAVĀDA             MĀDHYAMIKA / ŚŪNYAVĀDA
subject-object duality is constructed     all things lack svabhāva
vijñapti-mātra: representation-only       dependent arising = emptiness
ālaya-vijñāna stores bīja tendencies      two truths: saṃvṛti / paramārtha
three natures: parikalpita,                tetralemma rejects is / is-not /
paratantra, pariniṣpanna                   both / neither as ultimate capture
CONVERGENCE: dissolve reification; DIFFERENCE: Yogācāra privileges purified cognition,
while Mādhyamika empties even consciousness and emptiness itself.
OBJECTIONS: flux cannot explain continuity | anātman weakens agency | śūnyatā is nihilism
REPLIES: causal series | dependent responsibility | emptiness denies self-nature, not function
ANSWER RAIL
common core -> twelve links -> momentariness -> five-skandha no-self
-> karma/memory reply -> four-school fork -> exact school comparison
-> objection/reply -> qualified verdict
CLOSE: Buddhism replaces substance with conditioned process; its schools progressively
debate whether external dharmas, cognition, or any intrinsic nature can be retained.
NYĀYA: valid knowledge and argument       VAIŚEṢIKA: inventory of reality
+---- NYĀYA–VAIŚEṢIKA ----+
realism + pluralism + liberation through truth
pramā -> objects correctly known -> false notions removed -> faults cease
karma-producing action ceases -> rebirth and pain cease -> APAVARGA.
PADĀRTHA: whatever is nameable and knowable
1 DRAVYA: earth, water, fire, air, ākāśa, time, space, self, mind
2 GUṆA: quality; depends on substance, does not itself possess quality/action
3 KARMA: motion/action in a substance
4 SĀMĀNYA: real universal, one-in-many
5 VIŚEṢA: ultimate particularity individuating eternal atoms and selves
6 SAMAVĀYA: eternal inherence; whole-parts, universal-particular, quality-substance
7 ABHĀVA: absence — prior, posterior, mutual, absolute
CAUTION: samavāya is not conjunction (saṃyoga), which is separable.
PRAMĀṆAS
+-> pratyakṣa: sense-object contact -> nirvikalpaka -> savikalpaka recognition
+-> anumāna: sign (liṅga/hetu) through vyāpti to sādhya
+-> upamāna: knowledge through similarity and prior description
+-> śabda: trustworthy utterance, ultimately āpta testimony
PERCEPTION TYPES: external/internal | ordinary/alaukika
alaukika: sāmānyalakṣaṇa, jñānalakṣaṇa, yogaja
ERROR is mislocation of a real qualifier: anyathākhyāti.
SVĀRTHĀNUMĀNA: inference for oneself | PARĀRTHĀNUMĀNA: demonstrated to another
five members:
1 pratijñā: hill has fire
2 hetu: because it has smoke
3 udāharaṇa: wherever smoke, fire — as kitchen
4 upanaya: hill has such smoke
5 nigamana: therefore hill has fire
pakṣadharmatā + vyāpti + uncontradicted application -> conclusion
HETVĀBHĀSA: savyabhicāra, viruddha, satpratipakṣa, asiddha, bādhita.
ASATKĀRYAVĀDA / ĀRAMBHAVĀDA: effect is a new beginning, not pre-existent as effect
causes: samavāyi (inherent) | asamavāyi (non-inherent) | nimitta (efficient)
earth/water/fire/air paramāṇu -> dyad -> triad -> gross composite
pralaya: composites dissolve; eternal atoms, selves, space, time remain
sṛṣṭi: Īśvara activates atoms according to adṛṣṭa/karma
TRAP: God orders atoms; God is not the material cause and atoms are not created ex nihilo.
ĀTMAN: eternal, many, all-pervasive substrate of cognition, desire and volition
MANAS: atomic inner sense linking self to one cognition at a time
ĪŚVARA: eternal omniscient efficient cause; author/teacher of Veda;
coordinates atoms and karmic deserts without abolishing individual agency
true knowledge -> doṣa removed -> pravṛtti ceases -> karma exhausted -> apavarga
apavarga = complete cessation of pain; classical Nyāya does not define it as Brahman-union.
UDAYANA ROUTES: kāryāt (effect) | āyojanāt (combination) | dhṛtyādeḥ (support)
padāt (word-use) | pratyayataḥ (trust) | śruteḥ (Veda) | vākyāt (sentences)
saṃkhyāviśeṣāt (number) | adṛṣṭāt (moral order)
OBJECTION: atoms + karma may make God redundant; bodies expose unequal suffering
REPLY: unconscious atoms/adṛṣṭa cannot intelligently initiate and allocate order
SĀṂKHYA: satkāryavāda, prakṛti material cause | NYĀYA: new effect from atoms
BUDDHISM: momentary process | NYĀYA: enduring substances and selves.
DEFINE realist-pluralist synthesis -> list seven categories with relations
-> four pramāṇas -> perception stages -> five-member inference
-> anyathākhyāti -> self/manas -> Īśvara proofs and objection
-> ārambhavāda + three causes -> atomistic creation cycle
-> apavarga -> compare Sāṃkhya/Buddhism -> qualified verdict
VERDICT: the system gains explanatory integration from realism and logical method;
its pressure points are inherence, the leap from order to God, and austere liberation.
SĀṂKHYA = SATKĀRYAVĀDA + TATTVA EVOLUTION + PLURAL PURUṢAS
v                                 v
PRAKṚTI                              PURUṢA
one, unconscious, productive         many, conscious, inactive witnesses
avyakta equilibrium of guṇas         uncaused, unchanging, non-agent
v
apparent association explains experience; discrimination ends bondage.
THREE PRAMĀṆAS: perception | inference | reliable testimony
prakṛti is inferred, not ordinarily perceived
finite effects require cause -> effects share common features
coordinated world requires common source -> evolutes need an unevolved ground
pleasure/pain/dullness in effects -> sattva/rajas/tamas in cause
PRAKṚTI: beginningless, unmanifest, independent material cause;
not “matter” alone, but psychophysical source of intellect, senses and elements.
SATTVA
lightness | illumination | pleasure
/        PRAKṚTI          \
/   equilibrium breaks     \
activity | stimulation | pain     inertia | obstruction | dullness
guṇas are constituents, not detachable qualities
mutual domination + support + production drive all manifest difference.
PRAKṚTI (1)
-> MAHAT / BUDDHI (2)
-> AHAṂKĀRA (3)
+-> sāttvika -> MANAS (4) + 5 JÑĀNENDRIYAS + 5 KARMENDRIYAS
+-> tāmasa  -> 5 TANMĀTRAS -> 5 MAHĀBHŪTAS
+-> rājasa supplies activity to both branches
PURUṢA (25) stands outside the evolute chain as witness
COUNT CONTROL: 1 prakṛti + 23 evolutes + puruṣa = 25 tattvas.
EFFECT PRE-EXISTS LATENTLY IN CAUSE
asadakaraṇāt: non-being cannot be produced
upādānagrahaṇāt: specific material cause is selected
sarvasambhavābhāvāt: not everything arises from everything
śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt: cause produces only what it has power to produce
kāraṇabhāvāt: effect shares nature of cause
pariṇāmavāda: real transformation of prakṛti
NYĀYA ārambhavāda: new effect | ADVAITA vivarta: apparent transformation.
PURUṢA EXISTS BECAUSE
composites serve another | experience needs conscious witness
objects of three guṇas require non-guṇa experiencer | liberation is conceivable
PLURALITY: births/deaths differ; sense capacities and actions are uncoordinated;
if one puruṣa, one person's liberation or pain would belong to all
CONTACT PROBLEM: inactive consciousness cannot literally touch unconscious prakṛti
analogies: blind-and-lame cooperation | magnet and iron
pressure remains: how does mere proximity begin purposive evolution?
AVIVEKA: buddhi's states are appropriated as “I” by reflected consciousness
experience + karmic dispositions -> repeated embodiment
tattva-jñāna / viveka-khyāti: “I am puruṣa, not prakṛti or its evolutes”
prakṛti has been seen -> ceases activity for that puruṣa -> KAIVALYA
ŚAṂKARA: unconscious prakṛti cannot act for an end; dualism cannot explain contact
SĀṂKHYA REPLY: teleology is immanent, as milk flows for calf; no creator is needed.
START with dualism and three guṇas -> prove prakṛti and plural puruṣas
-> draw exact 25-tattva cascade -> defend satkāryavāda with five reasons
-> distinguish pariṇāma from ārambha/vivarta
-> explain aviveka and kaivalya -> test contact and teleology objections
QUALIFIED VERDICT: Sāṃkhya powerfully unifies cosmos, mind and liberation,
but the coordination of inactive consciousness with unconscious nature is its hard problem.

topics.title: Notions of God

lines: NOTIONS OF GOD
v
What kind of reality is called “God”, and how is it related to man and the world?
nature: personal / impersonal / transpersonal
attributes: power / knowledge / goodness / eternity / simplicity
relation: God-world / God-man / transcendence / immanence
NATURE AXIS: personal <-> impersonal | RELATION AXIS: transcendent <-> immanent
cataphatic affirmation + apophatic negation -> analogical control
too much affirmation = anthropomorphism | too much negation = empty God-talk.
WESTERN NOTIONS
+-> THEISM: personal necessary Creator; distinct, sustaining, providential
+-> DEISM: creation -> natural law -> withdrawal; miracles/revelation weakened
+-> PANTHEISM: God = world/nature
+-> PANENTHEISM: world is in God, but God exceeds world
+-> PROCESS/DIPOLAR GOD
abstract pole: eternal possibilities + stable character
consequent pole: receives changing world and experience
persuasion protects freedom, but revises omnipotence and immutability.
ATTRIBUTES: omnipotence | omniscience | goodness | eternity
immutability | simplicity | necessity | aseity
omnipotence -> logically possible acts; contradictions are not objects of power
foreknowledge vs freedom -> Boethius | Ockham | Molinism | open theism
goodness + power + knowledge + evil -> joint compatibility pressure
simplicity -> no parts; essence = existence; attributes not separable components
objection: can identical attributes permit free, personal relation to changing creatures?
DEUS SIVE NATURA -> ONE INFINITE SUBSTANCE
v                                 v
ATTRIBUTES: infinite expression          MODES: finite minds and bodies
humans know Thought and Extension        depend on the one substance
everything follows necessarily; God does not choose to create
radically immanent, not a personal ruler outside nature
objection: personality, providence and free will disappear
reply: freedom = self-determined action from one's own nature, not arbitrary choice.
ONE NON-DUAL BRAHMAN
+-> NIRGUṆA: beyond limiting predicates; pāramārthika; Sat-Cit-Ānanda
+-> SAGUṆA ĪŚVARA: personal Lord; creator/ruler; vyāvahārika; devotion
Brahman + māyā -> experienced world through VIVARTA, apparent transformation
rope appears snake; Brahman undergoes no real change
ĀTMAN = BRAHMAN -> liberation knows an already-existing identity
TRAP: anirvacanīya properly marks māyā/world appearance, not nirguṇa Brahman itself.
VIŚIṢṬĀDVAITA -> personal saguṇa Brahman, Nārāyaṇa
CIT (selves) + ACIT (matter) = real qualifications of Brahman
ŚARĪRA-ŚARĪRĪ: world/souls are body; Brahman is indwelling controller
APṚTHAK-SIDDHI: inseparable dependence without numerical identity
God = material and efficient cause; world is real PARIṆĀMA
jīva -> dependence -> bhakti -> prapatti -> liberation
objection: do bodily defects taint God? reply: defects belong to controlled body.

source_session_heading_references: FINAL REGISTER 7/10 — Other Indian and plural forms
lines: NYĀYA ĪŚVARA: God + selves + atoms + space/time are real
God is efficient cause; eternal atoms are material causes
karma/adṛṣṭa -> divine coordination -> fitting results; selves remain distinct
“IS HINDUISM POLYTHEISTIC?”
polytheism | henotheism | kathenotheism | monotheism | monism
Ṛgveda 1.164.46: reality is one; sages speak of it variously
verdict: many-deity practice, one-deity praise, sectarian supremacy and
Upaniṣadic monism coexist; one label cannot exhaust all levels.

source_session_heading_references: FINAL REGISTER 8/10 — Comparison and physical manifestation
lines: SYSTEM       GOD-WORLD                    GOD-MAN
Theism      creator and sustainer          worship, providence, grace
Deism       creator who withdraws          remote rational source
Spinoza     God = Nature                   person is finite mode
Advaita     world is vivarta               ātman = Brahman
Rāmānuja    world is God's real body       distinct yet inseparably dependent
Nyāya       God orders eternal atoms       distinct soul under moral governance
ultimate cause need not be physical: spatial/material dependence limits ultimacy;
pantheism and Rāmānuja qualify this without requiring an anthropomorphic body.
TRAPS: personal != anthropomorphic | transcendent != spatially remote
immanent != pantheistic | pantheism != panentheism | nirguṇa != non-existent
apṛthak-siddhi != identity | Nyāya God = efficient cause | monism != monotheism
PYQ ROUTES
personal/impersonal -> theism + Spinoza + saguṇa/nirguṇa
Spinoza -> substance -> attributes -> modes -> necessity -> criticism
Rāmānuja -> cit/acit -> body-soul -> apṛthak-siddhi -> devotion
freedom/God -> foreknowledge problem -> named solutions -> qualified verdict.

source_session_heading_references: FINAL REGISTER 10/10 — Advanced reserve and traps
lines: define exact God-concept -> state metaphysical model
-> explain God-world and God-man relations -> use exact school terminology
-> strongest objection -> strongest reply -> same-axis comparison
-> qualified philosophical verdict
God is a family of models: perfect person, infinite substance, non-dual consciousness,
organic unity or intelligent ordering. Adequacy turns on nature + attributes + relations
+ coherence: whether ultimacy best preserves agency, unity, devotion, independence,
moral order and intelligibility without contradiction.

topics.title: Proofs for the Existence of God and their Critique

source_session_heading_references: Register 1 — The architecture of theistic proof
lines: THEISTIC ARGUMENTS START FROM DIFFERENT DATA
+-> concept of God -> ONTOLOGICAL (a priori)
+-> contingent/moved/caused world -> COSMOLOGICAL (a posteriori)
+-> order and purposiveness -> TELEOLOGICAL
+-> objective obligation -> MORAL
+-> Indian effect/order/language/karma -> NYĀYA-UDAYANA
CONTROL: proofs may be deductive, abductive or cumulative;
never judge all by the standard of a single demonstrative syllogism.
ANSELM: God = that than which nothing greater can be conceived
existing in reality > existing only in understanding
therefore the greatest conceivable being exists in reality
DESCARTES: necessary existence belongs to supremely perfect being
MODAL FORM: possibly necessary God -> necessarily God, if S5 possibility is granted
GAUNILO: perfect-island parody | KANT: existence is not a real predicate
reply: necessary being is unlike contingent islands; pressure shifts to coherent possibility.
AQUINAS: motion -> unmoved mover | efficient causes -> first cause
contingency -> necessary being; not “every event has a cause”
KALĀM: whatever begins has a cause; universe began; therefore a cause
LEIBNIZ: principle of sufficient reason -> why something rather than nothing?
HUME: causal principle may not extend beyond experience; universe may be brute
RUSSELL: universe is “just there”; composition fallacy
REPLY: argument concerns contingent totality's explanation, not a member-cause in time.
PALEY: complex purposive adaptation -> watchmaker analogy -> designer
FINE-TUNING: life-permitting constants appear within narrow range
rival explanations
+-> design
+-> physical necessity
+-> chance / multiverse + selection effect
+-> unknown deeper law
HUME: weak analogy, many designers, imperfect designer | DARWIN: adaptation by selection
verdict: modern design is probabilistic/abductive, not Paley's biological inference unchanged.
KANT: morality does not theoretically prove God
highest good (virtue proportioned to happiness) -> practical postulates:
freedom + immortality + God
contemporary route: objective moral obligations -> adequate personal ground
objection: Euthyphro dilemma; secular realism can ground moral facts
reply: modified divine command grounds obligation in commands flowing from good nature
limit: the move from normativity to one religiously specified God remains underdetermined.
UDAYANA'S ROUTES TO ĪŚVARA
kāryāt: world as effect -> maker        āyojanāt: atomic combination -> arranger
dhṛtyādeḥ: support/dissolution          padāt: conventional word-use
pratyayataḥ: trustworthy cognition      śruteḥ/vākyāt: Vedic discourse
saṃkhyāviśeṣāt: determinate magnitudes  adṛṣṭāt: karmic allocation
ĪŚVARA = omniscient efficient cause; eternal atoms = material causes
not creation ex nihilo; proof aims at intelligent coordination of a realist cosmos.

source_session_heading_references: Register 7 — Jaina, Buddhist, Mīmāṃsā and Cārvāka critiques
lines: CĀRVĀKA: no perception of God; inference overreaches
BUDDHIST: momentary dependent series needs no permanent creator
JAINA: beginningless jīva/ajīva and karma; creation makes God responsible for evil
MĪMĀṂSĀ: Veda is authorless; dharma/apūrva explains ritual fruit without divine author
HUME/KANT: causal/design inference exceeds categories or experience
NYĀYA REPLY: unconscious atoms, apūrva or karma cannot intelligently allocate order
COUNTER: coordination may show explanatory gap, not uniquely the Nyāya God.

source_session_heading_references: Register 8 — Comparative synthesis and answer architecture
lines: DEFINE target God -> classify argument -> formalise premises -> expose hidden bridge
-> strongest named critic -> best reply -> test what conclusion actually establishes
ontological: necessity if possibility | cosmological: ground if PSR
design: probability, not deduction | moral: practical/normative support
Nyāya: intelligent order within atomism
QUALIFIED VERDICT: no proof compels every rational agent; together they can form a
cumulative case only if their contested modal, causal, probabilistic and moral premises stand.

topics.title: Problem of Evil

source_session_heading_references: A. Argument forms at a glance
lines: EVIL
+-> moral: freely caused cruelty, oppression, betrayal
+-> natural: disease, earthquake, congenital suffering
+-> horrendous: suffering that threatens life's overall meaning
+-> animal/evolutionary: pain predating human agency
PROBLEM TYPES
logical: God and evil are strictly inconsistent
evidential: amount/kinds of evil make God improbable
existential: suffering disrupts trust, worship and meaning.

source_session_heading_references: A. Argument forms at a glance
lines: CLAIMED SET: omnipotent God + omniscient God + perfectly good God + evil exists
missing premise: a good, powerful being eliminates every evil it can
PLANTINGA FREE-WILL DEFENCE
significant freedom -> possibility of moral wrong
God cannot cause a creature to choose freely and guarantee only right choices
transworld depravity shows logical possibility of unavoidable misuse
RESULT: compatibility is defended; actual quantity of evil is not thereby explained.
IRENAEUS / JOHN HICK
epistemic distance + stable natural laws + risk -> genuine agency
struggle -> courage, compassion, responsibility -> person-making
strength: addresses why a ready-made paradise may defeat mature freedom
objections: victims used as means; suffering is excessive and uneven;
infants, animals and horrors do not reliably improve sufferers
reply requires afterlife fulfilment/universal restoration, which adds further commitments.
AUGUSTINE: evil is privatio boni, not a created substance; misuse of freedom disorders good
LEIBNIZ: best possible world balances laws, freedom and total compossibility
AQUINAS: God may permit evil for a greater good, never will evil as evil
PROCESS THEISM: God persuades but cannot unilaterally prevent every event
COSTS: privation does not lessen felt horror; “best” can seem complacent;
greater-good reasoning risks instrumentalising victims; process view revises omnipotence.

source_session_heading_references: A. Argument forms at a glance
lines: ROWE: apparently pointless suffering exists; an omnipotent good God would prevent it;
therefore God's existence is improbable
hidden fawn case tests gratuitous natural suffering without human freedom
SKEPTICAL THEISM: limited human cognition cannot infer “no reason” from “no reason seen”
CORNEA: absence of evidence is evidence only where detection should be expected
objection: too much scepticism also weakens providential and moral reasoning
verdict must weigh epistemic humility against the specificity of apparently gratuitous evil.
ADVAITA: suffering belongs to vyāvahārika avidyā; ultimate Brahman is non-dual
VIŚIṢṬĀDVAITA: real souls/world, karma, grace and purposeful divine order
NYĀYA: beginningless karma allocated by Īśvara; God is not arbitrary author of deserts
JAINA: karmic matter binds jīva; no creator bears responsibility
BUDDHISM: duḥkha from dependent origination, craving and ignorance; no creator problem
KARMA explains moral continuity but faces first-origin, victim-blaming and natural-evil pressures;
liberation routes answer suffering therapeutically, not always as a theodicy.
TEST ANY THEODICY AGAINST
child suffering | animal pain | genocide | disability | unequal opportunity | hiddenness
ASK: does response explain, merely defend logical possibility, or offer pastoral meaning?
does it preserve victim dignity? does it make preventable evil morally acceptable?
anti-theodicy warning: neat justification can repeat harm
reply: philosophical explanation need not command passive acceptance;
moral protest may itself express commitment to goodness.
DEFINE God-concept + evil type -> separate logical/evidential/existential demand
-> formal argument -> strongest defence/theodicy -> hard-case objection
-> Indian comparison on karma/duḥkha -> qualified verdict
10 marks: one problem + one response + evaluation
15 marks: logical/evidential distinction + two responses
20 marks: Western and Indian matrix + hard cases + concept revision
CLOSE: evil may not disprove every God-concept, but it severely tests classical omni-God
belief and forces costs in freedom, providence, power, afterlife or human understanding.

topics.title: Soul, Immortality, Rebirth and Liberation

lines: SOUL = alleged enduring subject | PERSONAL IDENTITY = what makes later person same
IMMORTALITY = survival of death | REBIRTH = new embodied existence
RESURRECTION = divine restoration of embodied person | LIBERATION = release from bondage
QUESTIONS MUST BE KEPT DISTINCT
what survives? -> by what continuity criterion? -> where/when? -> through whose agency?
-> is survival endless life, renewed embodiment, or freedom from rebirth?
TERM CONTROL prevents treating Plato, Buddhism, Vedānta and Christianity as one doctrine.

source_session_heading_references: B. Immortality - Plato and the West
lines: PLATO
cyclical argument: opposites arise from opposites
recollection: a priori knowledge suggests prenatal existence
affinity: invisible rational soul resembles unchanging Forms
Phaedo final argument: soul essentially bears life and cannot admit death
objections: pre-existence != endless survival; harmony analogy; dependence on brain
DESIRE/JUSTICE ARGUMENTS: fulfilment or moral completion suggests afterlife
limit: wish and moral need do not by themselves establish metaphysical survival.

source_session_heading_references: B. Immortality - Plato and the West
J. Resurrection vs Rebirth vs Reincarnation
lines: IDENTITY CANDIDATES
+-> same immaterial substance
+-> bodily continuity / resurrection
+-> memory and psychological continuity (Locke)
+-> causal narrative continuity
REID: brave officer exposes memory transitivity problem
duplication: one psychology copied twice cannot yield two numerically identical persons
resurrection requires divine re-identification of this person, not mere replica production
verdict depends on whether identity needs strict sameness or survival-grade continuity.

source_session_heading_references: D. Buddhist Continuity Without a Soul
lines: INDIAN REBIRTH: karma + saṃskāra/vāsanā -> renewed embodiment in saṃsāra
BUDDHISM DENIES ĀTMAN
five skandhas + dependent origination -> causal stream -> rebirth without transmigrant
flame-to-flame: neither numerically identical nor wholly unrelated
intention conditions later fruit; memory is causally produced cognition
objection: who receives karma? reply: demand for substance mistakes continuity for identity
nirvāṇa ends craving and the causal appropriation that renews birth.
SCHOOL             BONDAGE                         LIBERATION
Advaita            avidyā, false identity           jñāna: ātman = Brahman
Viśiṣṭādvaita      karma, dependence obscured       bhakti/prapatti; communion
Sāṃkhya-Yoga       puruṣa-prakṛti confusion         kaivalya through viveka
Nyāya              false knowledge, doṣa, karma     apavarga: cessation of pain
Jainism             karmic pudgala on jīva           kevala-jñāna, siddhahood
Buddhism            craving/ignorance                nirvāṇa
Christianity       sin/death                         resurrection and salvation
SAME WORD “release” conceals different selves, causes, methods and end-states.

source_session_heading_references: G. Jain Jiva and Bondage Ladder
lines: ADVAITA: subtle body carries karma until knowledge; jīvanmukti possible;
videhamukti ends embodiment, not the ātman's existence
VIŚIṢṬĀDVAITA: jīva remains real and distinct; grace, bhakti and prapatti lead to God
JAINISM: jīva + passions/activity -> āsrava -> bandha
saṃvara blocks influx -> nirjarā sheds karma -> kevala-jñāna -> mokṣa
contrast: Advaita removes ignorance of identity; Rāmānuja perfects dependence;
Jainism purges material karma from an eternally individual soul.

source_session_heading_references: H. Cessation and Isolation - Apavarga, Jivanmukti, Kaivalya
I. Paths - Bhakti and the Three Means
lines: THREE BROAD MEANS: jñāna (knowledge) | bhakti (devotion) | karma (disciplined action)
Yoga adds meditative discipline; Jainism adds vows/austerity; Buddhism eightfold path
objections: disembodied soul lacks individuation | rebirth lacks memory
liberation as painlessness seems empty | endless survival may be burden, not good
replies: character/causal continuity can outlast episodic memory;
liberation is evaluated by freedom from ignorance, craving or sin, not mere duration
ethical test: doctrine should transform present conduct, not postpone justice to another life.
DEFINE exact survival term -> identify bearer and continuity criterion
-> explain causal mechanism -> state soteriological end and path
-> strongest objection (identity, evidence, justice) -> strongest reply
-> compare one unlike doctrine on same axes -> qualified conclusion
ANSWER AXES: self/no-self | body/disembodiment | karma/grace | continuity/identity
| endless existence/release from existence
CLOSE: survival doctrines are credible only when their ontology of the person,
continuity mechanism and ethical-liberative purpose support one another.

topics.title: Reason, Revelation and Faith

lines: REASON: publicly assessable inference, coherence and evidence
REVELATION: claimed divine self-disclosure through event, person, text or experience
FAITH: trusting commitment with cognitive, volitional and practical dimensions
v                     v
reason tests interpretation     revelation supplies content
v
faith appropriates a claim in life; it is not merely low-evidence assent.
REASON AND FAITH
+-> CONFLICT: one defeats the other (strong rationalism / fideism)
+-> INDEPENDENCE: distinct domains or language-games
+-> DIALOGUE: mutual questions, analogies and correction
+-> INTEGRATION: one coherent account; natural and revealed theology cooperate
EXAM RULE: identify which reason, which faith and which claim;
scientific mechanism, metaphysical ground and salvific meaning need not compete directly.
GENERAL / NATURAL: creation, conscience, universal reason
SPECIAL: historical act, prophet, incarnation, scripture
PROPOSITIONAL: truths communicated | PERSONAL/EVENT: God disclosed in encounter/history
AUTHENTICATION TESTS
internal coherence | moral fruits | historical credibility | communal continuity
fit with prior knowledge | capacity to disclose rather than merely confirm desire
circularity problem: scripture authenticates God while God authenticates scripture.
ONE TRUTH, TWO ROUTES
truths accessible to reason: that God exists, some attributes, natural law
mysteries above reason: Trinity, Incarnation; not contrary to reason
grace perfects nature; revelation guides reason where inquiry is difficult or salvation urgent
contradiction cannot be genuinely divine because truth cannot conflict with truth
objection: imported metaphysics may domesticate revelation
reply: reason does not generate mystery; it removes contradiction and clarifies implication.
OBJECTIVE UNCERTAINTY + INFINITE PERSONAL CONCERN -> SUBJECTIVE APPROPRIATION
Kierkegaard: faith is passionate commitment, not a theorem forced by detached proof
Abraham exposes the “teleological suspension of the ethical” problem
belief-that: propositional assent | belief-in: trust and allegiance
faith may exceed available proof without affirming contradiction
objection: leap licenses fanaticism | reply: authentic faith entails inward risk,
responsibility and transformation, not arbitrary immunity from criticism.
SCIENCE asks repeatable natural mechanism; religion may ask ground, value and destiny
conflict arises when sacred interpretation makes empirical claims or scientism makes total claims
HUME ON MIRACLES: proportion belief to evidence; false testimony is usually more probable
than violation of uniform experience
REPLIES: assess specific event, independent witnesses, background probability and divine context
TESTIMONY is indispensable but defeasible; miracle cannot be inferred merely from anomaly.
EVIDENTIALISM: belief should match publicly available evidence
REFORMED EPISTEMOLOGY: belief in God may be properly basic unless defeated
WITTGENSTEINIAN VIEW: faith has grammar within a form of life
INDIAN PARITY
śruti/śabda as testimony | yukti as reasoning | anubhava as realisation
Advaita: scripture initiates inquiry; reasoning removes contradiction;
knowledge culminates in direct realisation
Nyāya: āpta testimony is a pramāṇa but must be semantically and causally trustworthy
Mīmāṃsā: authorless Veda avoids dependence on a divine speaker.
DEFINE all three terms -> select conflict/independence/dialogue/integration model
-> distinguish revelation type -> named thinker -> strongest objection and reply
-> Indian śruti-yukti-anubhava comparison -> practical and public implications
avoid “faith versus reason” as a slogan: ask whether faith is contrary,
above or supported by reason
QUALIFIED VERDICT: faith needs neither reduction to proof nor exemption from criticism;
rationally responsible faith is interpretive trust answerable to coherence,
evidence and moral fruit.

topics.title: Religious Experience: Nature and Object

lines: RELIGIOUS EXPERIENCE
1 PHENOMENOLOGY: what is it like?
2 OBJECT: what is experienced — God, the Holy, Brahman, emptiness, unity?
3 EPISTEMIC FORCE: does seeming-to-encounter justify belief?
TYPES: mystical unity | numinous encounter | conversion | prayer/worship
| revelatory vision | non-dual awareness
CONTROL: intensity and sincerity establish occurrence, not automatically veridical object.
JAMES'S MARKS OF MYSTICAL EXPERIENCE
INEFFABILITY: cannot be adequately stated
NOETIC QUALITY: felt as insight or knowledge
TRANSIENCY: usually brief
PASSIVITY: received rather than fully produced by will
“fruits, not roots”: assess transformation in life, not only origin theory
authority is strongest for experiencer, not coercively binding on outsiders
plural experiences support openness, but diverse objects complicate doctrinal proof.
THE NUMINOUS = MYSTERIUM TREMENDUM ET FASCINANS
mysterium: wholly other, beyond ordinary grasp
tremendum: awe, majesty, creature-feeling, dread
fascinans: attraction, grace, compelling value
“Holy” includes non-rational numinous depth plus moral/rational development
SACRED != automatically God: an object, place or event may mediate the Holy
objection: description can reify culturally trained emotion into an external object.
ADVAITA: aparokṣānubhūti is immediate knowledge of non-dual Brahman
not subject seeing divine object; subject-object division is sublated
śravaṇa -> manana -> nididhyāsana -> liberating knowledge
RADHAKRISHNAN: integral intuition discloses spiritual unity and grounds tolerance
strength: experience is transformative and non-inferential
pressure: ineffability vs doctrinal description; private certainty vs public adjudication;
Advaita interpretation may be one conceptual construction among religious traditions.
MODEL                WHAT EXPERIENCE PRESENTS
personal theism      an addressive “Thou,” grace, command, presence
Otto                 numinous Holy / wholly other
Advaita              non-dual Brahman; no final subject-object split
Buddhism             emptiness, cessation or suchness without creator
naturalism           altered brain/body state interpreted religiously
SAME phenomenological report may underdetermine ontology;
object-claim needs interpretation beyond raw immediacy.
SWINBURNE PRINCIPLE OF CREDULITY: accept seeming appearance unless defeated
PRINCIPLE OF TESTIMONY: generally trust reports unless there is reason not to
DEFEATERS: drugs/pathology | contradiction | prior implausibility | unreliable setting
positive checks: coherence | moral fruit | intersubjective fit | predictive/explanatory value
ALSTON: socially established doxastic practice may confer prima facie justification
objection: incompatible religious practices cannot all validate exclusive objects unchanged.
FREUD: wish-fulfilment | MARX: social consolation | neuroscience: neural correlate
pluralism: contradictory interpretations | ineffability: no communicable evidence
replies: causal explanation does not equal debunking; all perception has neural correlates;
fruits and disciplined practices may distinguish mature experience from fantasy
prayer/worship test object-relations: petition, gratitude, surrender, contemplation
public use must be modest: experience may justify commitment without authorising coercion.
DEFINE type -> describe phenomenology with James/Otto -> specify claimed object
-> distinguish experience from interpretation -> apply credulity/testimony and defeaters
-> compare Advaita/theism/Buddhism -> strongest naturalist or pluralist objection
-> reply -> qualified public verdict
CLOSE: religious experience is significant evidence within a life and practice,
but its object is not read straight off the feeling; interpretation and defeater control remain.

topics.title: Religion without God

lines: CAN RELIGION EXIST WITHOUT A CREATOR GOD?
religion may organise:
ultimate concern | sacred value | ritual | community | moral discipline
worldview | transformation | liberation
THEISM is sufficient for many religions, not conceptually necessary for all
test a tradition by doctrine + practice + soteriology, not by a Western creator template
TRAP: non-theistic != atheistic; silence, irrelevance and denial are different positions.
ATHEISM: denies that God exists
AGNOSTICISM: suspends judgement because knowledge/evidence is insufficient
NON-THEISM: God is absent or non-central to the path
ANTI-THEISM: holds God-belief harmful or false in a stronger evaluative sense
IGNOSTICISM: “God” must be made meaningful before existence is debated
practical atheism: life organised without reference to God
keep epistemic suspension separate from metaphysical denial.
FOUR NOBLE TRUTHS -> dependent origination -> eightfold path -> nirvāṇa
no eternal creator is needed; suffering has conditioned causes, not divine decree
devas may occur in cosmology but are impermanent and unsaving
Buddha rejects speculative questions when they do not conduce to cessation of duḥkha
objection: karma/order functions like hidden providence
reply: causal-moral regularity is impersonal; no omnipotent allocator or creator follows.
JAINISM: eternal jīva/ajīva; karmic matter; tīrthaṅkara teaches, not creates
MĪMĀṂSĀ: authorless eternal Veda; ritual action generates apūrva; no divine author needed
SĀṂKHYA: prakṛti evolves for plural puruṣas; unconscious teleology without creator
shared anti-creator pressure: if God is perfect, why create? if embodied, who made body?
distinctions: Jainism retains worshipful exemplars; Mīmāṃsā centres dharma/ritual;
Sāṃkhya centres discriminative metaphysics and kaivalya.
CĀRVĀKA denies God, afterlife, karma, Vedic authority and mokṣa
embodied this-worldly flourishing replaces salvation
DOES IT COUNT AS RELIGION?
doctrinal-historical member of Indian philosophical debate: YES
sacred/transcendent/soteriological practice in robust sense: largely NO
limit case shows that “philosophy without God” is easier than “religion without God”;
Buddhism/Jainism better preserve ritual, community and liberation functions.
“GOD IS DEAD” = collapse of the Christian-metaphysical value horizon
danger: nihilism, herd morality exposed, no transcendent guarantor
task: revaluation of values -> self-overcoming -> life-affirmation
not a simple empirical proof that no deity exists
objection: self-created values risk arbitrariness or domination
reply: genealogy tests inherited values; affirmative creation accepts responsibility
POST-THEISM asks what religious depth survives after classical supernatural belief.
RELIGIOUS NATURALISM: nature is ultimate; awe, gratitude, ritual and ethics without supernaturalism
FICTIONALISM: participate in God-language/practice without literal ontological assent
SEA OF FAITH / non-realism: religious symbols shape life rather than report a transcendent entity
objections: worship without real object is make-believe; prayer loses address; truth is sacrificed
replies: symbols and communal narratives can disclose value and transform conduct
pressure remains: can function alone preserve religion's claim to truth and transcendence?
DEFINE religion by clustered features -> distinguish four negative positions
-> demonstrate Buddhism/Jainism/Mīmāṃsā/Sāṃkhya -> use Cārvāka boundary
-> Nietzsche/post-theism -> naturalism/fictionalism -> objection on truth/object
VERDICT BY CRITERION
creator-belief necessary? NO | ultimate concern/ritual/transformation possible? YES
personal worship and providence preserved? often NO
CLOSE: religion without God is coherent, but not religion without any ultimate value,
disciplined practice, communal form or account of transformation.

topics.title: Religion and Morality

lines: RELIGION AND MORALITY
+-> DEPENDENCE: morality requires God/revelation
+-> INDEPENDENCE: moral truth is autonomous
+-> SUPPORT: morality is independent but religion motivates/sustains it
+-> TENSION: religious command or identity can conflict with moral judgement
separate ontology (what makes right), epistemology (how known),
motivation (why act) and sanction (reward/punishment); one answer need not settle all four.
GOD COMMANDS X -> X IS OBLIGATORY
attractions: objective authority | categorical demand | accountability | motivation
versions:
voluntarist: rightness constituted by command
epistemic: revelation tells us independently grounded moral truth
motivational: love/judgement strengthens compliance
pressure: command identification, conflicting revelations, autonomy and arbitrariness.
IS X GOOD BECAUSE GOD COMMANDS IT?
+-> YES: morality appears arbitrary; cruelty could become right
+-> NO: goodness is independent; God is not its foundation
MODIFIED DIVINE COMMAND THEORY
God's necessarily loving/good nature grounds value
divine commands flowing from that nature ground obligation
reply blocks arbitrary commands; objection asks whether “good nature” is intelligible
without a standard logically prior to command.
KANT: moral law arises from rational autonomy, not heteronomous reward or threat
categorical imperative -> universal law + humanity as end
God and immortality are practical postulates of highest good, not sources of duty
NATURAL LAW: practical reason reads goods and purposes in human nature;
Aquinas joins rational participation in eternal law with divine order
contrast: obey because rationally right, not merely because commanded;
religion may complete moral hope without replacing moral deliberation.
MĪMĀṂSĀ: dharma known through authorless Veda; apūrva links ritual act and result
NYĀYA: God administers karma, but deserts arise from agents' acts
BUDDHISM: intention, compassion and non-harm within dependent origination; no creator
JAINISM: ahiṃsā and vows purify jīva by blocking karmic influx
GĪTĀ/VEDĀNTA: dharma, niṣkāma karma, devotion and knowledge reshape agency
Indian ethics shows objective discipline without one uniform divine-command model.

source_session_heading_references: F. Why be moral all the time?
lines: WHY BE MORAL?
fear of punishment -> hope of reward -> social belonging -> character/virtue
-> respect for persons -> compassion -> love of good/God
lower motives may secure compliance but not moral maturity
religiosity can support self-control, service and forgiveness;
it can also rationalise bias when identity outruns universal concern
TEST: conduct and reasons, not ritual profession alone, reveal moral integration.
RELIGION WITHOUT MORALITY: ritual purity or orthodoxy detached from justice/compassion
VIOLENCE PATH: exclusive truth + sacred authorisation + dehumanised out-group
+ political grievance -> moral disengagement
safeguards: interpretation, conscience, rights, plural institutions, non-violence
NIETZSCHE: genealogy exposes ressentiment and life-denying slave morality
objection to Nietzsche: power may erase equality and protection of weak
verdict: both religion and anti-religious critique need independent scrutiny of consequences.
STATE precise dependence claim -> separate ground/knowledge/motive/sanction
-> DCT -> Euthyphro -> modified DCT -> Kant/natural law
-> Indian non-theistic and theistic models -> conduct/violence test -> verdict
CLOSE: morality need not depend on divine command for intelligibility,
yet religion can deepen moral motivation, community and hope;
its legitimacy depends on whether faith remains answerable to reason, dignity and justice.

topics.title: Religious Pluralism

lines: RELIGIOUS DIVERSITY OCCURS ALONG FOUR AXES
truth: contradictory doctrinal claims
salvation: who can attain liberation/salvation?
epistemic status: are others reasonable/justified?
civic status: what freedom and equality are owed?
PLURALISM can answer one axis without answering all
tolerance is a political/moral practice; it is not yet a metaphysical claim
that all religions are equally true.
EXCLUSIVISM: one tradition alone has saving truth
INCLUSIVISM: one norm is final, but grace/truth operates beyond explicit membership
PLURALISM: multiple traditions are valid responses/routes to ultimate reality
strengths: exclusivism preserves determinate truth; inclusivism widens salvation;
pluralism explains diversity and supports humility
costs: exclusion | patronising absorption | flattening real contradictions
each model must state truth criterion, salvation criterion and view of disagreement.
THE REAL AN SICH (noumenal, beyond full conceptual capture)
culturally shaped human responses
+-> personal representations: God, Allah, Īśvara
+-> non-personal representations: Brahman, nirvāṇa, emptiness
religions assessed by transformation from self-centredness to Reality-centredness
KANTIAN distinction explains diversity without declaring all propositions identical
objections: Hick imposes a meta-theory; the Real becomes unknowable; transformation test is vague.
ADVAITA: one Brahman; differences belong to empirical standpoint;
many paths may prepare for non-dual knowledge
RĀMĀNUJA: real plurality within Brahman's unity; devotion to personal God remains final
RĀMAKṚṢṆA/VIVEKĀNANDA: diverse religious paths can realise one ultimate
ABSOLUTE-TRUTH PROBLEM
if all views are partial, is “all are partial” itself absolute?
reply requires standpoint discipline, not effortless equivalence of incompatible claims.
ANEKĀNTAVĀDA: reality has many aspects
NAYAVĀDA: each finite statement arises from a standpoint
SYĀDVĀDA: predicate conditionally — in a certain respect
pluralist use: rival religions may disclose different aspects without exhaustive possession
strength: epistemic humility + non-violence in judgement
limit: contradictions are reconciled only if respects genuinely differ;
syādvāda cannot simply pronounce every doctrine true in the same sense.
TOLERANCE: refrain from coercion despite disagreement
respect: recognise equal standing | dialogue: reciprocal reason-giving
freedom: belief, practice, change of religion, non-belief, association
LIMITS
coercion | violence | discrimination | harm to rights may be regulated
but offence or theological falsity alone is not sufficient ground for suppression
principled pluralism protects persons and conscience, not every practice from criticism.
CONFLICT SOURCES: exclusive revelation | sacred history | identity | power | grievance
responses: syncretism | common ethical core | comparative theology | dialogue | legal neutrality
DEEP DISAGREEMENT persists because standards of evidence are tradition-shaped
humility != relativism: give reasons, admit fallibility, seek overlap, preserve dissent
objections to pluralism: self-refuting, imperial meta-theory, doctrinal dilution
reply: modest pluralism can defend equal civic respect without equalising every truth claim.
DEFINE axis -> map exclusivism/inclusivism/pluralism -> explain Hick exactly
-> compare Advaita/Rāmānuja/Jain anekānta -> test absolute-truth objection
-> move from metaphysical diversity to tolerance/freedom with limits
-> qualified conclusion
CLOSE: defensible pluralism is neither “all religions say the same” nor relativism;
it combines truth-seeking, fallibilism, transformative comparison and equal civic liberty.

topics.title: Religious Language

lines: RELIGIOUS LANGUAGE HAS TWO DISTINCT QUESTIONS
AXIS 1 — MODE OF PREDICATION: univocal | equivocal | analogical | symbolic | negative
AXIS 2 — LOGICAL STATUS: cognitive/factual | non-cognitive | performative | expressive
“God is good” may be analogical AND cognitive;
“I commit myself to God” may be meaningful without describing an observable object
NEVER merge how words mean with whether utterances assert facts.
UNIVOCAL: same meaning for God and creatures -> clarity, but risks anthropomorphism
EQUIVOCAL: wholly different meaning -> protects transcendence, but blocks knowledge/inference
ANALOGICAL: related meaning grounded in causal participation
AQUINAS: analogy of attribution/proportionality; creaturely goodness reflects divine source
SCOTUS: some univocal concept of being is needed for valid reasoning about God
tension: enough continuity for truth, enough difference for transcendence.
TILLICH: symbol participates in the reality it discloses and opens levels of reality/self
symbols are living and can die; they are not arbitrary signs
VIA NEGATIVA: God is not finite, composite or dependent
PSEUDO-DIONYSIUS: affirmation -> negation -> supereminent transcendence
INDIAN “NETI NETI”: not this, not this; removes finite objectification
LAKṢAṆĀ/indication: indirect meaning when literal sense fails
limit: pure negation must retain some positive orientation or reference disappears.
COGNITIVE REALISM: God-talk states truths that may be warranted or false
ANTI-REALISM/NON-REALISM: language expresses a form of life, orientation or construction
EXPRESSIVISM: articulates attitude/commitment
PERFORMATIVISM: prayer, vow, confession and blessing do something
MYTHIC/NARRATIVE: forms identity and discloses a world of meaning
utterances can have several functions; functional richness does not itself settle reference.
AYER: cognitively meaningful factual claims must be analytic or empirically verifiable
-> traditional God-talk appears meaningless, not merely false
HICK: eschatological verification — celestial-city parable; confirmation may occur after death
FLEW: believers let “God loves us” die by a thousand qualifications
HARE: religious blik is unfalsifiable orientation yet meaningful
MITCHELL: partisan trusts stranger despite counter-evidence; commitment remains evidentially tested
key test: what counts against the claim, and what kind of claim is it?

panels.panel_title: 6. Use, self-involvement and forms of life
lines: WITTGENSTEIN: meaning is use within a language-game and form of life
prayer, lament, confession and worship are not failed scientific hypotheses
BRAITHWAITE: religious assertions express intention to follow an agapeistic way of life
SAME WORD, DIFFERENT GRAMMAR
“father” biological/secular | “Father” relational religious use
“creation” temporal manufacture | dependence on ultimate source
objection: use may explain intelligibility, but cannot by itself guarantee truth
or protect critique.
MYSTICISM: ineffability pressures literal description; paradox and symbol point beyond concepts
ADVAITA: nirguṇa Brahman beyond limiting predicates; saguṇa language valid empirically
mahāvākya interpretation uses implication to remove incompatible literal attributes
PLURALISM: different conceptual schemes may refer to or construct diverse ultimates
challenge: translation without erasing doctrinal difference
answer: compare reference, predication, function and life-context separately.
